report:
test_total does not fail. It passes. The failing test is test_half_cent_rounds_up.

Test run (python -m pytest): 2 passed, 1 failed.
- test_plain: pass
- test_total: pass (10% off 399 = 359.1, int() gives 359, expected 359)
- test_half_cent_rounds_up: FAIL, assert 959 == 960

Why it fails: cart.total ends with int(subtotal * (1 - discount_percent / 100)).
int() cuts off the fraction (truncates toward zero). It does not round.
5% off 1010 = 959.5, int() gives 959, the test expects 960.
This is the same bug as the TODO item "customers see totals one cent short".
test_total passes only because 359.1 truncates and rounds to the same number.

Note for a fix (not made, you asked a question): Python round() uses half to even
(round(959.5) = 960 but round(958.5) = 958), and the float 1 - 5/100 can give values
like 959.4999. For cents, integer math with half up is safer, for example
(subtotal * (100 - discount_percent) + 50) // 100.

No files changed except this report.
